# NeoForge mod workflow

These rules sit on top of the `minecraft-modding` skill. That skill has the code patterns; this one decides versions, lookups, pacing and verification. Where they disagree, this one wins.

## Scope

- NeoForge only. If a request needs Fabric, Forge or a multiloader setup, say so and stop.
- Supported Minecraft versions:

| Version | Java | Mappings | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26.1 (default for new mods) | 25 | None. 26.x is unobfuscated and uses official names. | Start from the current NeoForge generator or MDK for that exact version. |
| 26.3 | 25 | None. | Same as 26.1. Check the NeoForge changelog for API changes since 26.1. |
| 1.21.1 | 21 | Mojang mappings plus Parchment. | NeoForge 21.1.x. Classes use `ResourceLocation`, not `Identifier`. |

- In an existing repo, the version is whatever `gradle.properties` says. Never change it, or any dependency version, unless asked.

## Looking things up

Never write an API name, method signature, registry name, event name or version number from memory. Check it first, in this order:

1. The `minecraft-modding` MCP server (adhi-jp), against the project's exact Minecraft version: `check-symbol-exists` or `batch-symbol-exists` before using a class or method, `get-class-source` and `get-class-members` to read vanilla code, `get-registry-data` for registry ids, `validate-access-transformer` after editing an access transformer, and `analyze-mod-jar` or `search-mod-source` for a dependency's API.
2. The NeoForge docs at `https://docs.neoforged.net` with the matching version selected, and the NeoForge changelog for that version.
3. Local clones under `~/DEV/git_repos` (see the `referencing-local-repos` skill), especially for addon APIs such as AE2.
4. The `minecraft-modding` skill's examples. Its `references/neoforge-api.md` is for 1.21.x only; for 26.x, use the sections labelled 26.x in `references/common-patterns.md`.

If a lookup fails and the answer still matters, say what could not be verified instead of guessing.

## Checkpoints

Work in small slices and stop at each checkpoint. Do not chain slices together without approval.

1. **Orient.** Read `gradle.properties`, the build script, `neoforge.mods.toml`, and the repo's `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `DEVELOPMENT.md` and `justfile` if present. Follow the repo's own conventions over this skill's.
2. **Plan, then stop.** Before writing code, give a short plan: what changes, which files, which existing classes are reused, how it will be verified, and any open question. Wait for approval.
3. **Implement one slice.** One feature or one coherent part of a feature, never the whole backlog.
4. **Verify the slice** (see below), then **stop and report**: what changed, what was verified and how, and what was not verified. Propose the next slice instead of starting it.

Always ask before:

- adding, removing or upgrading a dependency, or editing `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle` or `gradle.properties`;
- deleting or renaming files, registry ids or config keys, because renames break existing worlds and configs;
- changing saved-data, attachment or data-component formats that existing worlds already contain;
- running `runClient` or `runServer`, which open long-running processes;
- anything the plan did not cover.

## Verification

Use the repo's `justfile` recipes when they exist; otherwise call Gradle directly.

| After | Run |
|---|---|
| Any Java change | `./gradlew build` (compiles and runs unit tests) |
| Gameplay logic: blocks, machines, recipes, entities, persistence | `./gradlew runGameTestServer`, plus each variant the repo's CI runs (for example optional-dependency flags) |
| Datagen providers changed | The repo's datagen task (`runData` or `runClientData`), then inspect the diff in the generated resources |
| Access transformer changed | `validate-access-transformer` through the MCP server, then a build |

Report failures with the actual error output. A slice that adds gameplay logic without a GameTest needs a stated reason.

Rules that apply to every slice:

- Server-authoritative logic. Validate every client packet.
- Client-only classes live in client packages and never load on a dedicated server.
- Every registered block or item gets its model, texture, language entry, loot table or recipe in the same slice. No missing textures or raw translation keys.
- Item state uses data components; world and entity state uses saved data or data attachments.

## Starting a new mod

For a new mod from an empty folder, copy `references/new-mod-prompt.md` (next to this file) into the new folder as `PROMPT.md`. Fill in its placeholders with the user rather than inventing them. The checkpoints above still apply: the design bible is the first checkpoint, then each MVP slice.

# Local shortcuts for building, testing, formatting and releasing Modular Planters. `just` lists them, and `just <recipe>` runs one.
#
# CI does not call just. The workflows in .github/workflows run the same Gradle tasks and tools/ scripts directly.

set shell := ["bash", "-euo", "pipefail", "-c"]

# Recipe arguments arrive as $1, $2 and so on, so variadic recipes forward them with "$@" and keep each argument intact.
set positional-arguments

[private]
default:
    @just --list --unsorted

# Recipes that call tools outside the JDK depend on this, so a missing tool stops the recipe before it starts. DEVELOPMENT.md says how to install each one.
[private]
require +tools:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    missing=()
    for tool in "$@"; do
        command -v "$tool" >/dev/null || missing+=("$tool")
    done
    if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
        echo "error: missing ${missing[*]}. See the Setup section of DEVELOPMENT.md." >&2
        exit 1
    fi

[doc('Compile, run the unit tests and build the jar into build/libs/')]
[group('gradle')]
build:
    ./gradlew build

[doc('Run the unit tests in src/test')]
[group('gradle')]
test:
    ./gradlew test

[doc('Run the in-game tests on a headless server, for example: just gametest -PnoAe2')]
[group('gradle')]
gametest *flags:
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer "$@"

[doc('Run the unit tests, then the in-game tests with all dev mods, without AE2 and without Applied Flux, the three ways CI runs them')]
[group('gradle')]
check:
    ./gradlew test
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAe2
    ./gradlew runGameTestServer -PnoAppliedFlux

[doc('Start a dev client, for example: just client -PnoPowah')]
[group('gradle')]
client *flags:
    ./gradlew runClient "$@"

[doc('Start a dev dedicated server')]
[group('gradle')]
server *flags:
    ./gradlew runServer "$@"

[doc('Regenerate src/generated/resources')]
[group('gradle')]
data:
    ./gradlew runData

# The first run updates gradle-wrapper.properties with the old Gradle, and the second run lets the new Gradle rewrite gradlew and gradle-wrapper.jar to match it.
[doc('Upgrade the Gradle wrapper, for example: just gradle-update 9.8.2')]
[group('gradle')]
gradle-update version:
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"
    ./gradlew wrapper --gradle-version "$1"

[doc('Run every pre-commit hook on every file, as CI does')]
[group('lint')]
lint: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure

# The formatters exit 1 when they rewrite a file, so a second run decides the result: it passes when the first run fixed everything.
[doc('Format the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place')]
[group('lint')]
fmt: (require "prek")
    prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier || prek run --all-files pretty-format-java prettier

[doc('Lint the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor')]
[group('ci')]
ci-lint: (require "actrun" "zizmor")
    actrun lint
    zizmor --offline .github/workflows

# local-ci runs the jobs in Docker with GitHub's own runner, against the working tree including uncommitted changes.
[doc('Run the Build workflow locally in Docker, for example: just ci -p to pause on a failed step')]
[group('ci')]
ci *flags: (require "local-ci" "docker")
    @docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "error: Docker is not running. Start Docker Desktop first." >&2; exit 1; }
    local-ci run --workflow .github/workflows/build.yml "$@"

[doc('Render the mod logo into docs/media/logo.png and src/main/resources/logo.png')]
[group('media')]
logo: (require "uv")
    uv run tools/render_logo.py

[doc('Compress PNG files in place, for example: just compress docs/media/*.png')]
[group('media')]
compress +files: (require "pngquant" "oxipng")
    pngquant --quality=80-95 --speed 1 --strip --force --ext .png "$@"
    oxipng -o 4 --strip safe "$@"

[doc('Print the changelog notes for one release tag, for example: just changelog 26.1.2-0.1.0')]
[group('release')]
changelog version:
    @bash tools/changelog-section.sh "$1"

[doc('Check that the version in gradle.properties is ready to tag, then dry-run the publish to GitHub, CurseForge and Modrinth')]
[group('release')]
release-check:
    bash tools/check-release.sh "$(bash tools/release-version.sh)"
    DRY_RUN=1 GITHUB_TOKEN=REDACTED ./gradlew publishMods

The `minecraft-modding` MCP is connected and works for vanilla lookups, but it can't find NeoForge classes unless you point it at a jar. `neoforge-mod-workflow` needs a fix for that.

The saved Recall context dates from 2026-10-29 (plan 1, old folder name), so I'm not relying on it.

## MCP status
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Connection | `minecraft-modding` is connected with all 41 tools, and `idea` tools are loaded too. |
| `just-mcp` | **Failed to connect.** It's configured in `~/.claude.json` and `just-mcp` isn't on PATH, but that cause is a guess. |
| `bunx` and Node | `bunx` 1.4.4 and Node 26.13.0 are on PATH. |

## Lookups against 26.1.2
| Lookup | Target | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `BlockEntity.preRemoveSideEffects`, which the mod overrides | `version` | Found, `(BlockPos, BlockState)V` |
| `BlockEntity` members | `version` | Works: `saveAdditional(ValueOutput)`, `loadAdditional(ValueInput)` |
| `block` registry | `version` | 1168 entries |
| `ModList` and `EnergyHandler` | `workspace` (`loader` and `merged` scopes) | **`ERR_CLASS_NOT_FOUND`**: both resolved to the vanilla artifact |
| `ModList` | `dependency` | **`ERR_CONTEXT_UNRESOLVED`**: the artifact has no binary jar |
| `EnergyHandler` | `jar` (NeoForge universal jar) | Works, 6 methods |

`ModList` is in the separate `fancymodloader` loader jar. I didn't run a jar lookup for it, or work out which of the cached loader versions this repo uses. I also didn't test `analyze-mod-jar` or `search-mod-source` for AE2. The problem is logged in `~/.config/papercuts.md`.

## How the skills split the work
- **`minecraft-modding`:** has the code patterns. For 26.x, use only the sections labelled 26.x in `common-patterns.md`; `neoforge-api.md` is legacy 1.21.x only, and `SKILL.md` says the same.
- **`neoforge-mod-workflow`:** sets versions, lookup order, checkpoints and verification, and wins any conflict with `minecraft-modding`. It also tells you to follow the repo's own conventions over its rules.

## What's outdated in the handoff
- The skill and the `.gitignore` edit are now committed, and `CLAUDE.md` has the project rules.
- `.mcp.json` now also defines `idea`.

## Workflow compared with this repo
- **Matches:** `just check` runs the unit tests plus the three GameTest variants in the CI matrix (none, `-PnoAe2`, `-PnoAppliedFlux`). `just data` is the datagen task.
- **Only in the repo's `CLAUDE.md`:** `just lint`, `just gametest -PnoJade` after Jade changes, and in-game checks for Jade and the Oracle Index. These are repo-specific, so they can stay there.
- **Conflict:** the workflow asks for `./gradlew build` after Java changes, while your global `CLAUDE.md` says not to rebuild unless asked.

## Questions for you
1. **Should I add the jar-target workaround to `neoforge-mod-workflow`?** I recommend yes: use `version` for vanilla and a `jar` target for NeoForge and FML classes. Without it, the skill's first lookup step fails on NeoForge classes.

3. **Do you want `just-mcp` fixed now?** I recommend leaving it, since the `justfile` recipes work from Bash without it.

content.text:
**Don't install `universal-modder`, but keep the clone as a read-only reference.** It's built for modding finished PC games of any engine through the running game, and NeoForge gets two lines in its Minecraft playbook. It wouldn't fix the NeoForge lookup problem either: it has no lookup tool and just points at the MCP you already run.

This comes from reading its source at commit `9811709`; nothing from it was installed or run, including its tests.

| | `universal-modder` | Current tools |
|---|---|---|
| **NeoForge 26.1.x** | No note targets it, and its skills still frame mappings around Loom and `genSources` | 26.x patterns and a version table |
| **API lookups** | None | Exact-version lookups through the MCP |
| **AE2** | One Fabric note saying no adapters were written | AE2 jar lookups work through the MCP |
| **Verification** | The running game is the test oracle | `just check`, GameTests and CI variants |
| **Pacing** | Runs from idea through to a recorded clip | One slice, then stop for approval |
| **Only here** | Field notes from other modders, asset generation, sprite pipeline, video editing, porting method | Access-transformer validation, optional-dependency GameTest variants |

**If you installed it:**
- **Conflicts with your rules:** it says to commit each working step and to treat `runClient` as the test oracle. Its `mod-any-game` trigger also overlaps `neoforge-mod-workflow`.
- **Failed server:** its `fal` MCP server fails to authenticate without `FAL_KEY`.
- **macOS:** `um win` refuses to run.
- **Low risk otherwise:** it adds one hook that only edits `PATH` and requests no permissions. A text search found no telemetry, but that isn't proof there is none.

**Worth keeping:** gotcha 19 in `knowledge/games/minecraft/neoforge-26-2-modpack-audit-perf-mods.md` lists API changes from 26.1 to 26.2, which helps if this mod moves up. It's a community note that hasn't been checked against the NeoForge changelog, and it doesn't cover 26.3.

## Correction to my lookup finding
I logged the jar target as the fix for NeoForge lookups, which was too narrow; the papercut log now has the correction. The research agent ran these:

| To read | Target |
|---|---|
| Vanilla | `version` |
| NeoForge source | `dependency` with explicit version `26.1.2.116` |
| NeoForge members | `jar` on the universal jar |
| FML `ModList` | `jar` on `loader-11.0.15.jar`, the version in the NeoForge pom |
| AE2 and other addons | `jar` on the jar in the Gradle cache |

Avoid `versionFromProject` on this machine: it fails when several versions are cached, and 16 NeoForge versions are. `analyze-mod-jar` and `search-mod-source` are still untested on AE2.

## Questions for you
1. **Should I add this target table to `neoforge-mod-workflow`?** I recommend yes, since `universal-modder` offers no alternative.
2. **After Java changes, should I run `just check` and `just lint`?** I recommend running them at the end of each slice and otherwise not rebuilding.

The full report is at `/Users/sweetjp/tmp/2026-11-05-universal-modder-research/universal-modder-comparison.md`. I kept it out of this repo because it contains private paths.

1	# Developing Modular Planters
2	
3	## Setup
4	
5	- JDK 25 on your `PATH`. Gradle 9.8.2 starts with JDK 17 or newer through the wrapper (`./gradlew`), and the build compiles with JDK 25, which Gradle can also download through the Foojay toolchain resolver. The Java formatter hook runs the `java` on your `PATH` and reads the code with that JDK's compiler, so it needs JDK 25.
6	- [just](https://just.systems) for the commands below and [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) for the pre-commit hooks: `brew install just prek`. Run `prek install` once in your clone. After that, each commit formats Java with google-java-format and Markdown, YAML and JSON with Prettier, then checks the workflows and shell scripts.
7	- Optional, for redrawing the logo with `just logo`: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (`brew install uv`). For compressing screenshots with `just compress`: `brew install pngquant oxipng`.
8	- Optional, for testing the GitHub workflows before pushing: Docker, `brew install zizmor`, and `bun add -g @mizchi/actrun run-local-ci`. `just ci` runs the Build workflow in Docker and `just ci-lint` lints the workflows.
9	- An IDE is optional. IntelliJ IDEA imports the project from `build.gradle`, and the `idea` plugin downloads sources and javadoc for Minecraft and NeoForge. `.editorconfig` sets Java to 2-space indents and 100 columns, matching google-java-format.
10	
11	The first build downloads Minecraft, NeoForge and the dev mods, so it takes a few minutes.
12	
13	## Commands
14	
15	Run `just` to list the recipes. Each one wraps a Gradle task or a script in `tools/`, so `./gradlew runClient` and the rest still work without just.
16	
17	| Command                        | What it does                                                                                              |
18	| ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
19	| `just build`                   | Compiles, runs the unit tests and builds the jar into `build/libs/`                                       |
20	| `just test`                    | Runs the unit tests in `src/test`                                                                         |
21	| `just gametest`                | Starts a headless server that runs the in-game tests in `src/main/java/.../gametest` and exits            |
22	| `just check`                   | Runs the unit tests, then the in-game tests with every dev mod, with `-PnoAe2` and with `-PnoAppliedFlux` |
23	| `just client`                  | Starts a dev client with the mod and the dev mods below                                                   |
24	| `just server`                  | Starts a dev dedicated server with no GUI                                                                 |
25	| `just data`                    | Regenerates `src/generated/resources` (recipes, loot tables, lang, models)                                |
26	| `just gradle-update <version>` | Upgrades the Gradle wrapper to that version                                                               |
27	| `just lint`                    | Runs every pre-commit hook on every file                                                                  |
28	| `just fmt`                     | Formats the Java, Markdown, YAML and JSON files in place                                                  |
29	| `just ci-lint`                 | Lints the GitHub workflows with actrun and zizmor                                                         |
30	| `just ci`                      | Runs the Build workflow locally in Docker with local-ci, uncommitted changes included                     |
31	| `just logo`                    | Redraws the logo from the block textures                                                                  |
32	| `just compress <files>`        | Compresses PNG screenshots with pngquant and oxipng                                                       |
33	| `just changelog <tag>`         | Prints the changelog notes for one release                                                                |
34	| `just release-check`           | Checks that the version is ready to tag, then dry-runs the publish                                        |
35	
36	Run `just check` and `just lint` before opening a pull request. After changing anything in `datagen`, also run `just data` and commit the result. The Build workflow runs all of these on every push and pull request, and fails if `runData` would change `src/generated`.
37	
38	## Where things live
39	
40	- `src/main/java`: the mod. The `gametest` and `datagen` packages are left out of the jar.
41	- `src/generated/resources`: output of `runData`. It is committed, so run `runData` and commit the result after changing anything in `datagen`.
42	- `wiki/`: the guide's pages. `processResources` copies them into the jar, where Oracle Index reads them as a book.
43	- `docs/description.md` and `docs/media/`: the CurseForge and Modrinth page and its images. World shots are JPEG. Screenshots of screens are PNG, compressed with `just compress <files>`, which runs `pngquant` and then `oxipng` (`brew install pngquant oxipng`). The logo PNGs are left as `tools/render_logo.py` writes them.
44	- `tools/changelog-section.sh`, `tools/check-release.sh` and `tools/release-version.sh`: the release checks that `just release-check` and the Release workflow run.
45	- `.github/workflows/`: `build.yml` runs `checks.yml` on every push and pull request, and `release.yml` runs it on a release tag before publishing.
46	- `tools/render_logo.py`: draws the logo from the block textures. Run `just logo` after changing a block texture, and commit both `docs/media/logo.png` and `src/main/resources/logo.png`.
47	
48	## Dev mods
49	
50	These are on the dev runtime (`runClient`, `runServer`, `runGameTestServer`) but not in the jar. Agritech: Evolved is the only required dependency. Each switch below leaves a mod out of a run, for example `just client -PnoAe2`.
51	
52	| Mod                | Version       | Comes with                     | Switch                                     |
53	| ------------------ | ------------- | ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------ |
54	| Agritech: Evolved  | 2.2.0.6       |                                | required                                   |
55	| Jade               | 26.1.12       |                                | `-PnoJade`                                 |
56	| AE2                | 26.1.13-beta  | GuideME 26.1.15-beta           | `-PnoAe2`                                  |
57	| Applied Flux       | 26.1-1.0.2    | Glodium 26.1-1.2               | `-PnoAppliedFlux`, also off with `-PnoAe2` |
58	| Powah              | 7.0.4-alpha   | Cloth Config 26.1.154, GuideME | `-PnoPowah`                                |
59	| Oracle Index       | 2.0.0         | Architectury 20.1.17           | `-PnoOracleIndex`                          |
60	| Logistics Networks | 26.1.2-1.13.0 |                                | `-PnoLogisticsNetworks`                    |
61	
62	The mod has code only for Jade, AE2 and Applied Flux. Powah is there for its fast FE source and cables. Oracle Index shows the guide, and Logistics Networks lets you test a node on the core. Most versions match the ones the All the Mods 11 modpack runs. Applied Flux isn't in that pack, and its AE2 build can differ.
63	
64	## Releasing
65	
66	A release tag is `<minecraft_version>-<mod_version>`, for example `26.1.2-0.1.0` or `26.3-0.2.0`. Pushing one runs the Release workflow. It checks the tag and runs the same checks as every push. Then it makes a GitHub release with the jar those checks built, and after that uploads the same jar to CurseForge and Modrinth.
67	
68	1. Set `mod_version` in `gradle.properties` to three numbers, such as `0.2.0`. A `-alpha` or `-beta` suffix, such as `0.2.0-beta`, publishes an alpha or a beta. Without one it is a full release.
69	2. Add a `## <tag>` section to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`, below the intro line. Its notes become the release notes on all three sites.
70	3. Run `just release-check`. It builds the tag from `gradle.properties`, fails if the tag has the wrong format or the changelog has no notes for it, then dry-runs the publish.
71	4. Commit, then run `git tag <tag> && git push origin main <tag>`.
72	
73	The workflow reads the repository secrets `CURSEFORGE_API_KEY` and `MODRINTH_API_KEY`, and the project ids `curseforge_project_id` and `modrinth_project_id` in `gradle.properties`. An empty id skips that site, and the run logs a notice saying so. The GitHub release uses the workflow's own token.
74	
75	If an upload fails, for example because a site is down, use "Re-run failed jobs" on that workflow run. A fix that needs a code change is released as a new version with a new tag. A tag that was pushed is never moved.
76	
77	## Screenshots with Structure Lab
78	
79	`-PstructureLabJar=<path to jar>` adds Structure Lab to a dev run. It places a structure file in a flat world and saves screenshots from set camera angles, which is how the world shots in `docs/media/` were taken. It is a local build that isn't published, so leave the switch out unless you have the jar. It needs a world created with the "Structure Lab" world type.
80

1	# Contributing to Modular Planters
2	
3	Contributions are welcome: bug fixes, compatibility fixes, guide corrections and code improvements.
4	
5	I have a specific vision for the mod and what content fits it. Before working on new content or a balance change, please open an issue and talk it through first, so your time isn't spent on something that won't be merged.
6	
7	## Issues
8	
9	- Search the open and closed issues first. Your bug or idea may already be there.
10	- Use the bug report or feature request form. For bugs, a log link and steps to reproduce make the biggest difference.
11	
12	## Pull requests
13	
14	- Make one pull request per change. Separate fixes are easier to review and to revert.
15	- Link the issue the pull request fixes.
16	- Say how you tested it. At least run `just check` and `just lint`, and check client-side changes in game and on a dedicated server.
17	- Run `prek install` once in your clone, so each commit is formatted the way the Build workflow checks it.
18	- Check your spelling and grammar in text players see, such as the guide in `wiki/` and the lang entries.
19	
20	[DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md) explains how to set up the project and run it locally.

# Modular Planters

NeoForge 26.1.2 addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE) that merges many planters into one multiblock. DEVELOPMENT.md has the commands, layout, dev mods and release steps. CONTRIBUTING.md has the pull request rules.

The repo is public, and each push also sends Entire session logs to `origin`, so keep private paths and personal details out of commits.

## Every task

- Run `just check` and `just lint` to verify a change.
- The mod must load with any optional mod missing.
- Don't rename save keys or registry ids, because that breaks existing worlds. The save key `soil_and_modules` keeps its old name, and ATE's own names stay as ATE has them.
- Never squash or rebase merged history, because `.git-blame-ignore-revs` names the reformat commit e1a9a58.
- Player-facing text uses the block names from `en_us.json`, "upgrades" instead of "modules", and "Advanced Planter" instead of "Powered Planter".

## Read before you work on

- [Verifying changes](docs/agents/verifying.md): datagen, the Jade variant, and what GameTests cannot prove.
- [Optional mods and the ME link](docs/agents/optional-mods.md): the `mod_loaded` conditions and the `MeLink` contract.
- [GameTests](docs/agents/gametests.md): assertion and mock player pitfalls.
- [Docs, wiki and store pages](docs/agents/docs-and-wiki.md): MDX, the link test, and the page images.
- [Build and tooling](docs/agents/build-and-tooling.md): CI cache provider, hook commands, `entire graph` limits and `./gradlew clean`.

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `GLOSSARY.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── GLOSSARY.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── GLOSSARY-MAP.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── GLOSSARY.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── GLOSSARY.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

Create files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `GLOSSARY.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `GLOSSARY.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?"

### Update GLOSSARY.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `GLOSSARY.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md](./GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md).

`GLOSSARY.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `GLOSSARY.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

# GLOSSARY.md Format

## Structure

```md
# {Context Name}

{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}

## Language

**Order**:
{A one or two sentence description of the term}
_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction

**Invoice**:
A request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.
_Avoid_: Bill, payment request

**Customer**:
A person or organization that places orders.
_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account
```

## Rules

- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.
- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.
- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.
- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.

## Single vs multi-context repos

**Single context (most repos):** One `GLOSSARY.md` at the repo root.

**Multiple contexts:** A `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:

```md
# Glossary Map

## Contexts

- [Ordering](./src/ordering/GLOSSARY.md): receives and tracks customer orders
- [Billing](./src/billing/GLOSSARY.md): generates invoices and processes payments
- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/GLOSSARY.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping

## Relationships

- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking
- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices
- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`
```

The skill infers which structure applies:

- If `GLOSSARY-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts
- If only a root `GLOSSARY.md` exists, single context
- If neither exists, create a root `GLOSSARY.md` lazily when the first term is resolved

When multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.
=====ADR
# ADR Format

ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily: only when the first ADR is needed.

## Template

```md
# {Short title of the decision}

{1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}
```

That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why*, not in filling out sections.

## Optional sections

Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.

- **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`): useful when decisions are revisited
- **Considered Options**: only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering
- **Consequences**: only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out

## Numbering

Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.

## When to offer an ADR

All three of these must be true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will look at the code and wonder "why on earth did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If a decision is easy to reverse, skip it: you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond "we did the obvious thing."

### What qualifies

- **Architectural shape.** "We're using a monorepo." "The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres."
- **Integration patterns between contexts.** "Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP."
- **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library: just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.
- **Boundary and scope decisions.** "Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only." The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.
- **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** "We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X." Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from "fixing" something that was deliberate.
- **Constraints not visible in the code.** "We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements." "Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract."
- **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it; otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.

1	# Modular Planters: design
2	
3	Date: 2026-10-28. Status: approved by the owner on 2026-10-28.
4	
5	Modular Planters is an addon for Agritech: Evolved (ATE). It lets a player replace dozens or hundreds of ATE Advanced Planters with a few multiblocks, while each one produces, draws and costs about what the same number of Advanced Planters would.
6	
7	Choices marked **(my call)** were made by Claude, the assistant writing this, and haven't been confirmed by the owner yet. Everything else was decided by the owner. The brainstorm record, with the research behind these numbers, is `NOTES.md` in the mod folder.
8	
9	## Why
10	
11	The owner's farm runs about 400 ATE Advanced Planters, mostly Mystical Agriculture seeds. 333 of them grow nickel for a reactor fuel line, each with 2 Speed Upgrade MK3s, insanium farmland and a cloche. Those nickel seeds are maxed in every Productive Farming trait (see "Seed traits"). Every planter needs its own seed, soil, two upgrades and a Logistics Networks (LN) node on three channels: energy in, fertilizer in, outputs out. Adding capacity means placing and configuring one more planter and one more node each time.
12	
13	The mod collapses this into a few multiblocks. A planter block holding 64 seeds stands in for 64 Advanced Planters. One connection to the multiblock's core replaces the per-planter nodes.
14	
15	## Goals
16	
17	- A planter block with N growing seeds produces what N Advanced Planters with the same seed, soil, upgrades and fertilizer produce, and draws the same power.
18	- A fully upgraded planter block costs about what 64 upgraded Advanced Planters cost.
19	- One connection to the core (an LN node, a cable, pipes, or the ME block) runs a whole multiblock.
20	- Planter blocks that can't be reached in a build can still be managed from the core's screen.
21	- It works in any modpack: it follows the pack's ATE config and recipes, and its own recipes are datapack recipes a pack can replace.
22	
23	## Non-goals
24	
25	- No new crops, soils, fertilizers or upgrade items. The mod uses ATE's own Speed and Yield Upgrades and ATE's own planter recipes.
26	- No dedicated Logistics Networks block. An ordinary LN node on the core does the job.
27	- NeoForge on Minecraft 26.1.2 only. No Fabric and no other Minecraft versions.
28	- No 3D scenes in the guide. Oracle Index doesn't support them, so example builds are still images.
29	
30	## Anti-goals
31	
32	These would make the mod a failure even if it worked:
33	
34	- A planter block out-producing the matching number of Advanced Planters, apart from the built-in cloche's yield rule below.
35	- Voiding items. When there's nowhere to put outputs, planter blocks wait.
36	- Requiring AE2, Applied Flux or Logistics Networks. All three are optional.
37	- Hard-coding ATE's default numbers. In game, every ATE number is read from ATE's live config.
38	- Copying code from ModularBees. ModularBees is LGPL-3.0 and this mod is MIT, so ModularBees may be read for ideas only.
39	
40	## Constraints
41	
42	- **Platform:** NeoForge, Minecraft 26.1.2. It must run in the FTB Evolution 2 instance (pack 1.5.1, NeoForge 26.1.2.121) at `~/.ftba/instances/ftb evolution 2`.
43	- **Dependencies:**
44	  - Hard: ATE (tested with 2.2.0.6).
45	  - Optional: AE2 (26.1.13-beta), Applied Flux (26.1-1.0.2), Logistics Networks (26.1.2-1.13.0), Oracle Index (2.0.0), Jade.
46	  - The mod has to load and work with any combination of the optional ones missing.
47	- **Identity:**
48	  - Mod name: Modular Planters.
49	  - Mod id: `modular_planters`.
50	  - Java package: `io.github.julianperge.modular_planters`.
51	  - GitHub repo: `julian-perge/ModularPlanters`.
52	  - Local folder: `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`, renamed from `ate-planter-multiblock` (my call).
53	- **License:** MIT, with every line of code written for this mod. Textures are adapted from ATE's, which are MIT, so ATE's copyright notice ships with the mod.
54	- **ATE config:** every ATE number is read through ATE's public static getters in `com.misterd.agritechevolved.Config`, for example `Config.getPlanterBasePowerConsumption()`, the same way the Advanced Planter reads them. ATE's defaults appear in this document only as worked examples. Tests may pin those defaults.
55	- **Logistics Networks tags:** no block in this mod may be in LN's blacklist tags (`logisticsnetwork:blacklist/block` and the item, fluid and chemical variants).
56	
57	## The blocks
58	
59	| Block | Job |
60	|---|---|
61	| Core | Forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche, opens the core screen, and acts as a doorway for energy, fertilizer and outputs. Stores nothing itself. |
62	| Power | Stores energy. The only place energy is kept. |
63	| Fertilizer | Stores fertilizer, shared by every planter block. |
64	| Export | Holds outputs until something pulls them out. |
65	| Planter | Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds. |
66	| ME | Optional, and only exists when AE2 is installed. Connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. |
67	| Frame | Does nothing except connect parts. |
68	
69	There's no import block. The fertilizer block covers that job.
70	
71	### Core
72	
73	- **It's a doorway.** While formed, the core exposes three capabilities:
74	  - **Energy:** energy inserted into the core goes to the power blocks.
75	  - **Fertilizer in:** items inserted into the core go to the fertilizer blocks. Only fertilizers are accepted.
76	  - **Outputs:** items extracted from the core come out of the export blocks.
77	  - So one LN node on the core with the owner's existing three-channel settings runs a whole multiblock. Each part block also exposes its own resource directly, so cables and pipes can connect to the power, fertilizer or export blocks instead.
78	- **While not formed**, the core exposes no capabilities (my call).
79	- **It applies the built-in cloche to every planter block.** The cloche is always on and needs no item. See "Built-in cloche".
80	- **Its screen** is described under "Core screen".
81	
82	### Power block
83	
84	- Stores energy. Several power blocks pool their storage (my call).
85	- Buffer: 4,000,000 RF each, the same as ATE's Capacitor Tier 3, which is its key recipe ingredient (my call). This is set in the mod's server config.
86	- Accepts energy at least as fast as the whole multiblock can draw it, with no low per-tick limit (my call). ATE's Tier 3 Capacitor moves only 8,192 RF/t, which wouldn't cover even one full planter block.
87	- Energy can't be extracted from it (my call).
88	- When broken, it keeps its stored energy in the dropped item, like ATE's capacitors (my call).
89	
90	### Fertilizer block
91	
92	- 27 slots (my call). Accepts only items in ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map.
93	- Several fertilizer blocks pool their contents (my call).
94	- Drops its contents when broken.
95	
96	### Export block
97	
98	- 54 slots (my call). Only the multiblock can insert. Anything can extract.
99	- Several export blocks fill one after another (my call).
100	- Drops its contents when broken.
101	
102	### Planter block
103	
104	The planter block's own behavior is described under "How a planter block grows".
105	
106	### ME block
107	
108	- Only exists when AE2 is installed: the block's registration, item and recipe are all conditional on AE2.
109	- It's an AE2 grid node that uses one channel. A multiblock can have at most one. A second ME block keeps the multiblock from forming, since it would do nothing (my call).
110	- **Outputs:**
111	  - Harvested outputs go straight into ME storage.
112	  - Whatever ME doesn't accept goes into the export blocks.
113	  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block also moves whatever is in the export blocks into ME (my call).
114	- **Fertilizer:**
115	  - The ME block's screen has one filter slot where the player picks a fertilizer.
116	  - Every 20 ticks, the ME block tops the fertilizer blocks up with that fertilizer from ME (my call).
117	- **Applied Flux:**
118	  - When Applied Flux is also installed, the ME block keeps the power blocks charged from the network's stored FE.
119	  - Each tick, before the planter blocks run, it fills the power blocks' free room from the network's FE, so they stay full and their bars show stored power. Filling empty power blocks takes up to their capacity, 4,000,000 RF each, out of the network once (owner ruling, 2026-10-30, after in-game testing: the earlier rule drew only what the planter blocks asked for the tick before, so the power blocks always showed 0 and looked broken).
120	  - Without Applied Flux, power comes in through the core or the power blocks.
121	  - A Flux Accessor placed against the core or a power block also works either way, with no code in this mod.
122	
123	### Frame block
124	
125	- Connects parts and does nothing else.
126	- It's also the in-between step when crafting a planter block (see "Recipes").
127	
128	## Structure
129	
130	- **Free form.** The multiblock is the core plus every part block connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact doesn't connect.
131	- **Size cap:** at most 24 parts, not counting the core. Frames count (my call).
132	  - Above the cap, the multiblock doesn't form, and the core's screen says why.
133	  - The cap is in the server config, default 24 (my call).
134	- **Required parts:** at least one power block, one export block and one planter block. Fertilizer, ME and frame blocks are optional.
135	- **Two cores:** if the connected parts reach a second core, neither forms. The core's screen names the problem block and its position (my call).
136	- **Re-checking:** the core re-checks the shape when a part next to the structure is placed or broken.
137	- **When the shape breaks:** the planter blocks stop, but every block keeps its contents.
138	
139	The guide shows three example builds from the brainstorm, saved in `mockups/layouts.html`. They're examples only, since any connected shape works:
140	
141	- **Raised bed under a cloche:** corner legs, a 3x3 bed and a 3x3 glass canopy.
142	- **Vertical farm:** a 2x2 tower with the core on the bottom floor and floors of planter blocks above it.
143	- **Rosette:** one block tall. The core is in the center, the other parts take the four diagonal corners, and planter blocks extend outward in four arms.
144	
145	## How a planter block grows
146	
147	### Contents
148	
149	The planter block's screen has four slots, all filled by hand. They can also be filled from the core's screen.
150	
151	| Slot | Holds |
152	|---|---|
153	| Seed | A seed bin: up to 64 seeds of one item type. Anything a Advanced Planter accepts, saplings included. See "Seed traits". |
154	| Soil | One soil type, up to 64. Anything in ATE's `agritechevolved:soil_modifiers` data map, including Mystical Agradditions cruxes. |
155	| Upgrade 1 | One ATE upgrade type (Speed or Yield, MK1 to MK3), up to 64. |
156	| Upgrade 2 | Same as upgrade 1. |
157	
158	- There's no fertilizer slot and there are no output slots. Fertilizer comes from the fertilizer blocks, and outputs go to the export blocks or ME.
159	
160	### Seed traits
161	
162	Other mods can change a seed through ATE's planter events. Productive Farming, which FTB Evolution 2 includes, gives seeds traits such as Growth and Yield. Each harvest can raise one trait, and ATE writes the changed seed back into the planter. Seeds whose traits differ don't stack. The owner chose that every seed in a planter block keeps its own traits, so a planter block matches the same number of Advanced Planters exactly:
163	
164	- **What the bin holds:** up to 64 seeds of one item type, each kept as its own stack of 1 with its own data. Seeds of the same item with different traits can go in together. Players moving from Advanced Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them.
165	- **How the slot looks:** on screen the bin looks like one slot showing the seed and the count. Hovering over it lists how many seeds have each trait combination (my call).
166	- **Bin order:** seeds stay in the order they were put in (my call). The seed numbering below follows that order.
167	- **Taking seeds out:** the builder decides how seeds are taken back out of the bin.
168	- **Each seed levels on its own,** exactly as it would in its own Advanced Planter.
169	- **No Productive Farming code:** all of this works through ATE's events, so Productive Farming isn't a dependency.
170	- The seed and soil must be a valid pair under ATE's planter recipes (`agritechevolved:crop` and `agritechevolved:tree`). The mod reads those recipes, so new ATE crops and KubeJS recipes work without changes.
171	
172	### Seeds, soil and upgrades
173	
174	- **Growing seeds:** G = the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. 64 seeds on 13 soil grow the first 13 in bin order. The other 51 are idle, and the screen says so.
175	- **One upgrade covers one seed.** Let A = the smaller of upgrade 1's count and G, and B = the smaller of upgrade 2's count and G. Number the growing seeds 1 to G. Seed i gets upgrade 1 if i is at most A, and upgrade 2 if i is at most B. So by upgrades the seeds fall into at most three sets:
176	  - The smaller of A and B: seeds with both upgrades.
177	  - The larger minus the smaller: seeds with only the fuller slot's upgrade.
178	  - G minus the larger: seeds with no upgrade.
179	- **Groups:** a group is a set of growing seeds with the same upgrade set and identical seed data, traits included. Seeds with different traits are in different groups even when they have the same upgrades.
180	- **Why seeds pair up this way (my call):** it matches a player filling Advanced Planters one at a time with both upgrades before starting the next.
181	- **The screen shows coverage:** "23/64 seeds upgraded" when upgrades run short, and "13 working, 51 idle" when soil runs short.
182	
183	### Growth
184	
185	Each group behaves exactly like that many Advanced Planters with that upgrade set, running in lockstep:
186	
187	- **Progress:** each group keeps its own progress counter.
188	- **Growth time:** recomputed every tick with ATE's formula: `max(1, round(advanced base processing time / (soil x upgrade speed x fertilizer speed x cloche speed)))`.
189	  - Upgrade speed uses ATE's Speed Upgrade multipliers and Yield Upgrade speed penalties, as in `AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity.getModuleSpeedModifier`.
190	  - Cloche speed is ATE's configured cloche speed bonus.
191	  - The planter block then fires ATE's `PlanterProcessingTimeEvent` once for the group, passing itself as the planter and one of the group's seeds. Every seed in a group has identical data, so one event speaks for all of them. The planter block uses whatever time the event returns. That's how Productive Farming's Growth trait applies.
192	- **Harvest:** when a group's progress reaches its growth time, the whole group harvests at once.
193	- **After a harvest,** seeds whose traits just changed form new groups. Every seed that harvested starts again at zero, so no progress is lost or gained.
194	
195	### Power
196	
197	- **Draw per tick:** for each group still growing, the number of seeds times `round(base power consumption x upgrade power multiplier)`. Only Speed Upgrades raise power, as in ATE's `getModulePowerModifier`.
198	- **When there isn't enough:** if the power blocks can't cover the planter block's full draw for a tick, no group in that planter block advances that tick. A planter block never runs only some of its seeds.
199	- **Who gets power first (my call):** planter blocks draw in a fixed order, sorted by block position. When power runs short, the same planter blocks keep running and the rest pause, so it doesn't flicker between them.
200	- **Waiting to harvest:** a group that's ready to harvest but waiting for output room draws no power, as in ATE.
201	
202	### Fertilizer
203	
204	Each growing seed uses fertilizer at ATE's rate, one item per harvest, so N seeds use what N Advanced Planters would.
205	
206	- **Which fertilizer (my call):** the fertilizer used is the item in the first non-empty slot of the fertilizer blocks, taken in a fixed order.
207	- **When a group counts as fertilized (my call, revised 2026-10-29 after the final review):** each tick, the fertilizer stored is a budget shared by every planter block of the core. Planter blocks claim from it in the same position order as power, and each group claims as many items as it has seeds, all or nothing. A group that claims is fertilized for that tick. A group that can't claim runs unfertilized that tick, so one stack can't speed up more seeds than it could pay for. A fertilized group uses the fertilizer's speed and yield multipliers from ATE's `agritechevolved:fertilizers` data map, and consumes one item per seed when it harvests. Otherwise the group runs unfertilized.
208	- **No fertilizer block:** if there's no fertilizer block, or it's empty, every planter block runs unfertilized.
209	
210	### Harvest and outputs
211	
212	When a group harvests, each seed in it goes through the same steps, in the same order as ATE's Advanced Planter (`AdvancedPlanterBlockEntity`, around line 584):
213	
214	1. Fire `PlanterPreHarvestEvent` for that seed, passing the planter block as the planter. Write the seed the event returns back into that seed's place in the bin. This is where Productive Farming raises a trait.
215	2. Roll that seed's drops from ATE's recipe, including chance drops, using the seed the event returned.
216	3. Apply ATE's yield rounding to each drop. This is r in "Built-in cloche".
217	4. Fire `PlanterPostHarvestEvent` for that seed with its own drop list. Productive Farming adds its Yield bonus to each stack in that list, so each seed must get its own event and its own list.
218	5. Add the cloche's kept fraction for each drop to the planter block's remainders. Extra items from the remainders are added after the event, never into the event's list, so per-stack bonuses from other mods never apply to them.
219	6. Insert the drops into ME, if there's an online ME block, and then into the export blocks.
220	7. Consume one fertilizer for that seed, if the group is fertilized.
221	
222	Output room (my call):
223	
224	- A group only starts harvesting if the export blocks, plus ME if it's online, have room for the group's drops as ATE's recipe lists them. This is like ATE's `hasOutputSpace`.
225	- Other mods can add to the drops during the events, so they may still not all fit. Whatever doesn't fit is held inside the planter block, and the planter block pauses until all of it has been moved out.
226	- Nothing is voided.
227	
228	### Built-in cloche
229	
230	The built-in cloche is always on and uses ATE's configured cloche speed and yield bonuses. They're 1.15 and 1.10 by default.
231	
232	**Speed:** the cloche speed bonus goes into the growth time formula above.
233	
234	**Yield:** ATE's Advanced Planter gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield x cloche yield))` for each drop. For a 1-item drop at 1.1 that rounds back to 1, so the cloche's yield bonus does nothing for Mystical Agriculture essence. The built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away. The owner decided this; it's the mod's one deliberate buff.
235	
236	The exact rule (my call, written so that it never gives less than ATE and never adds more than the cloche's own share):
237	
238	1. For each drop, let x = count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield, and e = x x cloche yield.
239	2. ATE's result is r = max(1, round(e)). The player always gets at least r.
240	3. The fraction kept is the smaller of (e - r) and x x (cloche yield - 1), or 0 if e - r is negative.
241	4. Add the kept fraction to a running remainder for that item, saved per planter block. Each time the remainder reaches 1, give one extra item and subtract 1.
242	
243	The yield bonus from other mods, such as Productive Farming's Yield trait, is added after this rule and never counts toward x or e.
244	
245	With the default 1.1 and a 1-item drop, each seed gets one extra every tenth harvest, a 10% gain. With a Yield MK3 (2.0), e is 2.2 and r is 2, so the cloche adds 0.2 per drop, again 10%. It also applies to seeds and fertilized essence, the same way ATE's yield bonus does (my call).
246	
247	### Changing contents mid-growth
248	
249	The builder decides how progress is kept when a player changes seeds, soil or upgrades mid-growth. The rule is that no change can produce a harvest earlier or larger than the same change to Advanced Planters would. Changing the seed or soil type resets progress, as in ATE.
250	
251	## Core screen
252	
253	The owner approved the layout in `mockups/core-screen.html`. It's modeled on the Logistics Networks Computer's Node Table (`LogisticsNetworks/src/main/resources/assets/logisticsnetworks/guides/logisticsnetworks/guide/computer/node-table.md`).
254	
255	- **Top bar:**
256	  - Formed state and part count, for example "FORMED 18 / 24".
257	  - When the multiblock isn't formed, the reason, naming the problem block and its position if there is one.
258	- **Totals:** stored power and current draw, fertilizer stored, how full the export blocks are, and ME status.
259	- **Planter table:**
260	  - One row per planter block, grouped by seed type under collapsible headings, the way LN groups nodes by label.
261	  - Each row shows:
262	    - the seed;
263	    - how many seeds are growing;
264	    - upgrade coverage;
265	    - a status: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle;
266	    - the block's position.
267	- **Row buttons:**
268	  - **Outline** toggles a glowing outline on that planter block in the world, visible only to that player, like LN's lamp button.
269	  - **Open** opens that planter block's screen remotely. It's the same screen as in the world, with a "Back to core" button added.
270	- **Rules:**
271	  - The table updates live.
272	  - Opening a planter block remotely is checked on the server: the player must be in range of the core, and the planter block must belong to that core's formed multiblock.
273	
274	## Integrations
275	
276	### Logistics Networks
277	
278	- There's no LN code in the mod. A node on the core works through the core's doorway capabilities.
279	- The node needs an upgrade sized to the multiblock. A node uses its best upgrade for every channel, and LN's default limits are:
280	
281	| Node upgrade | Energy per tick | Items a second |
282	|---|---|---|
283	| None | 2,000 RF | 0.8 |
284	| Iron | 10,000 RF | 64 |
285	| Gold | 50,000 RF | 256 |
286	| Diamond | 250,000 RF | 5,120 |
287	| Netherite | about 2.1 billion RF | 200,000 |
288	
289	- Example with ATE's defaults: a full planter block of 64 nickel seeds with 2 Speed Upgrade MK3s, insanium farmland and the built-in cloche.
290	  - **Power:** it draws 32,768 RF/t whatever the seeds' traits.
291	  - **Items:** with seeds that have no traits, it puts out about 24 items a second. With seeds maxed in Productive Farming's Growth and Yield, like the owner's, it puts out about 320 items a second. That's more than a gold upgrade moves.
292	  - **Upgrade needed:** a diamond upgrade covers up to 7 such planter blocks, and power is the limit. More than 7 needs a netherite upgrade, or more nodes on the power blocks.
293	- The guide has to include this table and example.
294	
295	### AE2 and Applied Flux
296	
297	See the ME block above. AE2 and Applied Flux are compile-time-only dependencies. All code that touches them sits behind a mod-loaded check, so the mod loads without them.
298	
299	### Productive Farming
300	
301	- There's no Productive Farming code in the mod. Its traits work through ATE's three planter events, fired as described under "How a planter block grows".
302	- It's in FTB Evolution 2, with `statsOnExternalCrops = true`, so Mystical Agriculture seeds gain traits there. Manual testing uses that pack.
303	
304	### Jade
305	
306	An optional Jade plugin (my call, the lowest priority in the mod):
307	
308	- On the core: formed state.
309	- On a planter block: growing seeds and status.
310	
311	### JEI
312	
313	No JEI plugin. The crafting recipes show up in JEI on their own, and the crops are ATE's own planter recipes, which ATE already shows.
314	
315	## Recipes
316	
317	These are shaped crafting recipes, shipped as datapack JSON so packs can replace them. The owner chose each key ingredient. The other ingredients and the grid patterns are my calls.
318	
319	| Block | Pattern | Key |
320	|---|---|---|
321	| Frame | `PPP` `PIP` `PPP` | P = ATE Advanced Planter (`agritechevolved:advanced_planter`), I = block of iron |
322	| Planter | `FFF` `FIF` `FFF` | F = Frame, I = ATE Infused Farmland (`agritechevolved:infused_farmland`) |
323	| Core | `IGI` `GCG` `IDI` | C = ATE Cloche Dome (`agritechevolved:cloche_dome`), G = glass (`#c:glass_blocks`), I = block of iron, D = block of diamond |
324	| Power | `IRI` `RCR` `IRI` | C = ATE Capacitor Tier 3 (`agritechevolved:capacitor_tier3`), R = block of redstone, I = block of iron |
325	| Fertilizer | `IBI` `BSB` `IBI` | S = ATE Fertilizer Spreader (`agritechevolved:fertilizer_spreader`), B = bone block, I = block of iron |
326	| Export | `IHI` `HSH` `IHI` | S = ATE Silo (`agritechevolved:silo`), H = hopper, I = block of iron |
327	| ME | `IFI` `FXF` `IFI` | X = ME Interface (`#ae2:interface`), F = fluix crystal (`#c:gems/fluix`), I = block of iron. Has a `neoforge:mod_loaded` condition on `ae2`. |
328	
329	The owner's reasoning:
330	
331	- **Progression:** a player builds their first Modular Planter in the mid to late game, when they already farm diamonds, emeralds and netherite.
332	- **Gating:** the power block carries the progression gate. Every multiblock needs one, and a Tier 3 Capacitor takes diamonds and emeralds.
333	- **Two-step planter block:** it takes 64 Advanced Planters, and splitting that into two steps keeps any one recipe from needing stacks of an item.
334	- **Following the pack:** using Advanced Planters means a pack that makes them cost more makes planter blocks cost more too. Players can also break existing Advanced Planters and craft them straight in.
335	- **Iron for the frame:** a frame used as filler costs 8 Advanced Planters, and an iron center keeps it from also costing 9 diamonds.
336	- **No frames in the other parts:** they aren't crafted from frames, which would add 8 Advanced Planters to each.
337	
338	## Textures and models
339	
340	- Every block is a full cube (my call).
341	- Textures are adapted from ATE's, in `AgritechEvolved/src/main/resources/assets/agritechevolved/textures/block/`, so the blocks look like part of ATE. For example:
342	  - the power block from the capacitor textures;
343	  - the core from the cloche dome textures;
344	  - the planter block from the planter textures.
345	- Planter blocks don't render their crops (my call). A planter block can switch between an "on" and an "off" texture while growing, the way ATE's capacitors do (my call).
346	
347	## Server config
348	
349	The mod's own server config holds (my call):
350	
351	- the part cap (default 24);
352	- the power block's buffer (default 4,000,000 RF);
353	- the ME block's export and fertilizer interval (default 20 ticks).
354	
355	ATE's numbers are never copied into this config. They're always read from ATE.
356	
357	## Guide
358	
359	The guide is an Oracle Index book, set up the way Oritech does it:
360	
361	- The pages live in a `wiki/` folder, using the moddedmc.wiki layout.
362	- `processResources` copies them into `assets/oracle_index/books/modular_planters`.
363	- Oracle Index is `compileOnly`, so it isn't needed at runtime.
364	
365	Pages:
366	
367	- An overview.
368	- One page per block, with its recipe.
369	- The building rules.
370	- The three example builds as still images.
371	- The planter block's seed, soil and upgrade rules.
372	- The built-in cloche rule.
373	- The Logistics Networks upgrade table and example.
374	- AE2 and Applied Flux.
375	
376	The Oritech repo at `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/Oritech` is the working example to copy the setup from.
377	
378	## Testing
379	
380	- **Unit tests** for the math:
381	  - grouping seeds by upgrade coverage;
382	  - the soil limit;
383	  - growth time and power draw per group;
384	  - fertilizer use;
385	  - the cloche yield rule.
386	  - One test checks that a planter block with N seeds gives the same expected output and power as N simulated Advanced Planters, using ATE's default numbers.
387	  - One test registers a listener on ATE's three events that acts like Productive Farming: it changes the seed and adds a flat bonus to each drop stack. The test checks that seeds level on their own, that each seed gets its own post-harvest event, and that the cloche's extra items never get the bonus.
388	- **NeoForge GameTests** for the world behavior:
389	  - forming and breaking;
390	  - the part cap and the two-core case;
391	  - missing required parts;
392	  - pausing for power and for full exports;
393	  - the core's doorway capabilities;
394	  - contents kept when the shape breaks.
395	- **Manual play** in the FTB Evolution 2 instance, including a Logistics Networks node on the core and an ME block with Applied Flux.
396	
397	## Left to the builder
398	
399	- **Build setup:** the Gradle setup, the NeoForge and Java versions within the constraints above, and the code structure.
400	- **Multiblock mechanics:** how forming and re-checking are triggered, and how the structure behaves across chunk borders and unloaded chunks. Whatever happens, items must never be lost or duplicated.
401	- **NeoForge 26.1 APIs:** how the doorway and part capabilities are wired with the transfer API that ATE already uses (`ResourceHandler<ItemResource>`, `ItemStacksResourceHandler`).
402	- **Screens:** the menu, screen and network code for the core screen and remote opening.
403	- **AE2 and Applied Flux:** how the ME block uses their APIs. ModularBees' `xmod/ae/` and the Applied Flux jar are references, read but not copied.
404	- **Changing contents mid-growth:** the exact progress rule, within the rule stated above. Seeds added mid-growth must not join a group's progress.
405	- **The seed bin:** how players take seeds back out of it.
406	- **Assets:** how the textures are edited, and how the guide's images are made.
407	
408	## Calls made without the owner
409	
410	These are listed together so the owner can check them:
411	
412	1. Parts:
413	   - several power blocks and several fertilizer blocks pool their contents, and several export blocks fill one after another;
414	   - the power block buffer is 4,000,000 RF, the fertilizer block has 27 slots, and the export block has 54.
415	2. Energy:
416	   - the power block accepts energy as fast as the multiblock can use it;
417	   - energy can't be extracted from it;
418	   - it keeps its energy when broken.
419	3. Structure rules:
420	   - the core exposes nothing while not formed;
421	   - frames count toward the cap, and the cap is in the server config;
422	   - a second ME block or a second core stops the multiblock from forming.
423	4. The ME block:
424	   - it moves export contents into ME every 20 ticks;
425	   - it tops fertilizer up every 20 ticks from one chosen fertilizer;
426	   - with Applied Flux, it keeps the power blocks full from the network's FE.
427	5. Upgrade coverage pairs both upgrades on the same seeds first.
428	6. Power: planter blocks are powered in a fixed order by position.
429	7. Fertilizer:
430	   - the first fertilizer found in the fertilizer blocks is the one used;
431	   - a group counts as fertilized only when there's enough for all its seeds.
432	8. Seed bin:
433	   - seeds keep the order they were put in;
434	   - hovering over the bin lists the trait combinations.
435	9. The exact cloche yield rule, applying it to every drop, and adding its extras after the post-harvest event.
436	10. Output room: a group starts harvesting when there's room for its listed drops, and anything other mods add that doesn't fit is held in the planter block until it's moved out.
437	11. Recipes: every ingredient and pattern other than the key ingredients.
438	12. Looks:
439	    - full cube blocks with no crop rendering;
440	    - an on and off texture for the planter block.
441	13. An optional Jade plugin, and no JEI plugin.
442	14. The server config contents.
443	15. The local folder `~/DEV/git_repos/minecraft-mods/ModularPlanters`.
444

input.content:
# Modular Planters

An addon for Agritech: Evolved that replaces many Advanced Planters with a few multiblocks. A block of N growing seeds produces, draws power and costs about what N Advanced Planters would.

## Language

### The multiblock

**Multiblock**:
A Modular Planter Core together with every part connected to it face to face, directly or through other parts. Diagonal contact does not connect.
_Avoid_: structure, machine

**Formed**:
A multiblock that meets the building rules and is running. A multiblock that is not formed keeps every block's contents but grows nothing.
_Avoid_: active, assembled

**Problem**:
The reason a multiblock is not formed, such as a second Core, too many parts, or a missing required part.
_Avoid_: error

**Part**:
Any Modular Planter block that joins a multiblock, other than the Core: Power, Fertilizer, Export, Planter, ME or Frame.
_Avoid_: module, component

**Modular Planter Core**:
The block that forms the multiblock, applies the built-in cloche to every Modular Planter Block, and opens the Core screen. It stores nothing itself.
_Avoid_: Planter Core, controller

**Doorway**:
The three resources a formed Core exposes to outside connections: energy in, fertilizer in, and outputs out.
_Avoid_: port, interface

**Modular Planter Power Block**:
Stores the multiblock's energy. Several Power Blocks pool their storage, and energy cannot be extracted from them.
_Avoid_: Planter Power, capacitor

**Modular Planter Fertilizer Block**:
Stores fertilizer for every Modular Planter Block in the multiblock. Several Fertilizer Blocks pool their contents.
_Avoid_: Planter Fertilizer, import block

**Modular Planter Export Block**:
Holds harvested outputs until something pulls them out. Only the multiblock inserts into it.
_Avoid_: Planter Export, output block

**Modular Planter Block**:
Grows one seed type, up to 64 seeds, from one soil type and up to two upgrade types.
_Avoid_: Planter Block, planter

**Modular Planter ME Block**:
An optional Part, present only when AE2 is installed, that connects the multiblock to an AE2 network. A multiblock can have at most one.
_Avoid_: ME interface, Planter ME

**Modular Planter Frame**:
A Part that does nothing except connect other Parts. It counts toward the part cap.
_Avoid_: Planter Frame

### Growing

**Seed**:
Any item an Advanced Planter accepts for planting, saplings included. Each seed carries its own data, such as traits added by other mods.

**Seed bin**:
The Modular Planter Block's seed slot. It holds up to 64 seeds of one item type, each with its own data, in the order they were added.
_Avoid_: seed stack

**Soil**:
The one soil type in a Modular Planter Block, up to 64 items. It limits how many seeds can grow.

**Upgrade**:
An ATE Speed or Yield upgrade item in a Modular Planter Block. One upgrade item covers one seed.
_Avoid_: module (ATE's own names and the `soil_and_modules` save key keep it)

**Growing seed**:
A seed that has soil to grow in. The number of growing seeds is the smaller of the seed count and the soil count. The rest are idle.
_Avoid_: active seed

**Upgrade coverage**:
How many growing seeds each upgrade slot reaches. Both slots cover the same seeds first, in bin order.

**Group**:
A set of growing seeds in one Modular Planter Block with the same upgrade set and identical seed data. A group grows and harvests together, like that many Advanced Planters in lockstep.
_Avoid_: batch, cohort, stack

**Fertilized**:
A group that claimed enough fertilizer for all its seeds that tick. A group that cannot claim runs unfertilized.

**Built-in cloche**:
The cloche effect every Modular Planter Block gets from the Core. It is always on, needs no item, and uses ATE's configured cloche bonuses.
_Avoid_: cloche dome (the Core's recipe ingredient)

**Remainder**:
The fraction of a yield bonus that ATE's rounding would discard. The built-in cloche carries it forward and adds one item each time it reaches a whole one.
_Avoid_: leftover, rounding bonus

**Held output**:
A drop that did not fit in the Export Blocks or ME. The Modular Planter Block pauses until all held outputs have moved out.
_Avoid_: overflow

**Status**:
What a Modular Planter Block is doing: growing, short on soil, paused for power, paused for a full export, or idle.

### Screens

**Core screen**:
The Core's screen. It shows the multiblock's totals and one row per Modular Planter Block, and can open any block's own screen remotely.
_Avoid_: controller screen

**Seed heading**:
A collapsible heading on the Core screen that lists Modular Planter Blocks by seed type.
_Avoid_: group

### Outside the mod

**Agritech: Evolved (ATE)**:
The mod this one extends. It owns the crops, soils, fertilizers, upgrades and the numbers everything is measured against.
_Avoid_: Agritech

**Advanced Planter**:
ATE's planter block, the baseline a Modular Planter Block must match.
_Avoid_: Powered Planter

**Optional mod**:
AE2, Applied Flux, Logistics Networks, Oracle Index or Jade. The mod loads and works with any of them missing.
_Avoid_: soft dependency, addon

**Guide**:
The in-game Oracle Index book that explains the mod.
_Avoid_: wiki, manual

# Seeds keep their own traits

Other mods, such as Productive Farming, change a seed through ATE's planter events, and seeds whose data differs do not stack. A seed bin holds each seed as its own item with its own data and groups seeds with identical data, so every seed levels on its own and a Modular Planter Block matches the same number of Advanced Planters exactly.

Players moving from Advanced Planters can put in all their seeds without sorting them, and the seed slot's tooltip lists how many seeds have each trait combination.

input.content:
# The built-in cloche keeps the rounded-away yield

ATE gives `max(1, round(count x fertilizer yield x upgrade yield x cloche yield))` for each drop, so a one-item drop at the default 1.1 cloche bonus rounds back to 1 and the bonus does nothing for single-item drops such as Mystical Agriculture essence. The owner decided the built-in cloche keeps the fraction that rounding throws away and pays one extra item each time it adds up to 1.

This is the mod's one deliberate buff. It never gives less than ATE and never more than the cloche's own share, and the extras are added after the post-harvest event so bonuses from other mods never apply to them.

input.content:
# Power and fertilizer are all-or-nothing, in block position order

If the Power Blocks cannot cover a Modular Planter Block's full draw for a tick, none of its groups advance that tick, so a block never runs only some of its seeds. Fertilizer works the same way per group: each tick the stored fertilizer is one budget shared by the whole multiblock, and a group either claims one item per seed or runs unfertilized, so one stack cannot speed up more seeds than it could pay for.

Blocks claim power and fertilizer in order of block position. When supply runs short, the same blocks keep running and the rest pause, instead of every block flickering on and off.
